title: Ammeter and voltmeter readings in a DC circuit with parallel and series resistors

question.statement: An ideal ammeter (zero resistance) and an ideal voltmeter (infinite resistance) are connected as shown. The ammeter and voltmeter reading for $R_{1} = 5\,\Omega$, $R_{2} = 15\,\Omega$, $R_{3} = 1.25\,\Omega$ and $E = 20\text{ V}$ are given as

figure_refs.caption: Circuit diagram with $R_1 = 5\,\Omega$ and $R_2 = 15\,\Omega$ in parallel, each branch containing a resistor, with an ammeter (A) in series with $R_1$. This parallel combination is connected in series with $R_3 = 1.25\,\Omega$, across which a voltmeter (V) is connected. The circuit is powered by an EMF source $E = 20\text{ V}$.
figure_refs.alt_text: Electrical circuit diagram with a DC voltage source E = 20 V. Two resistors R1 = 5 ohms (with ammeter A in series) and R2 = 15 ohms are connected in parallel. This parallel block is connected in series with R3 = 1.25 ohms. A voltmeter V is connected in parallel across the R1-R2 parallel combination.
